Detailed method

The calculator opens at 400 g flour, 50% hydration, 1.8% salt, and 1.6% yeast. The balls fields open at 1 piece of about 614 g, one loaf from this batch. Knead in about 80 g of soft butter, about 20% of the flour weight, and 1 egg. Butter and egg are not in the gram total. Braid it. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast into a stiff dough. At 50% hydration it feels dry. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Enrich Soften about 80 g of butter to about 20°C (68°F). Knead in 1 egg and the butter, a little at a time, until the dough is smooth and glossy. This takes about 10 to 15 minutes. The 80 g and the egg are not in the gram total.
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 1.6% yeast it should grow by about half.
  4. Chill Refrigerate the covered dough for 1 to 2 hours so the butter firms and the braid holds its shape.
  5. Braid Divide into three strands, roll them, and braid them. Pinch the ends and tuck them under. This is one loaf.
  6. Proof Set the braid on a sheet. Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 45 to 70 minutes, until it looks puffy. Brush with a little beaten egg (extra, not in the gram total).
  7. Bake Bake at 180°C (355°F) for 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is deep gold. If the top colors early, lay a loose piece of foil over it.
  8. Cool Cool on a rack for at least 45 minutes before you slice.
